items.quote: After thermal analysis, the alloys were examined by x-ray powder diffractometer Siemens D 5000 (Co K␣-radiation, step 0.02⬚ of 2⌰, and time in the point: 3 s) to identify the phases present.

The sample was sealed under pure argon at 1 bar in specially adapted tantalum containers using electric arc welding. This procedure entirely eliminated evaporation and oxidation of the samples during the long DTA runs. These DTA-sized containers with 9 mm diameter and 12 mm height were prepared with a highly reproducible weight (empty) of 2.23 ⫾ 0.03 g, including the tantalum lid. As reference, Al2O3 in another Ta crucible was used. Differential thermal analysis was performed using a Netzsch DTA differential thermal analyzer 404. Heating and cooling rates of 1 K/min were used. No reactions with the crucibles were observed. Several heating and cooling runs were performed. The temperature difference of the observed signals after repeated runs were below 2 K.

items.quote: In order to validate that reaction and to determine the invariant temperature of E1 by DTA, a sample of the composition 41 at.% Gd and 29 at.% Mg was prepared by arc melting the pure elements under argon atmosphere. Starting materials were gadolinium bulk material (99.95 mass%, Auer-Remy, Hamburg), lithium bulk material (99.9 mass%, Chemetall, Frankfurt), and magnesium pieces (99.98 mass%, Alfa Aesar, Karlsruhe). The elements were weighed, mixed, and then pressed under a pressure of 100 MPa into small pellets of around 1 g. The alloy was prepared by electric arc melting under argon atmosphere.
